name: GMX v1 GLP reentrancy short-price manipulation
summary: PositionManager.executeDecreaseOrder wraps order execution in enableLeverage/disableLeverage and refunds native ETH to the order account, which can be a contract; the refund re-enters mid-flow while leverage is enabled, letting the attacker open Vault shorts that drive shortsTracker.globalShortAveragePrices far below spot. GlpManager.getAum prices GLP from that reentrancy-manipulable global-short average with no manipulation resistance, so GLP minted before and redeemed after the manipulation over-withdraws the Vault's reserves.
notes: PositionManager is a direct, non-proxy contract (EIP-1967 implementation slot zero, no code change). The reentrancy is inherent to executeDecreaseOrder wrapping the order in enableLeverage/disableLeverage and refunding native ETH to an arbitrary account; no parameter value makes the deployed code correct, so deployment is the age basis. Its runtime hash is byte-identical at the creation block and immediately before the anchor.

GlpManager is a direct, non-proxy contract (EIP-1967 implementation slot zero, no code change). getAum/getGlobalShortAveragePrice price GLP from a live global-short average price that can be manipulated within one transaction via reentrant short opens. The shortsTrackerAveragePriceWeight parameter (10000 at exploit time, selecting shortsTracker.globalShortAveragePrices) only chooses which manipulable average is read; vault.globalShortAveragePrices is equally reentrancy-manipulable, so no parameter value removes the defect and deployment is the age basis. Runtime hash is byte-identical at the creation block and immediately before the anchor.

The measured loss is the net decrease of the GMX Vault's nine external reserve assets during the drain transaction 0x03182d3f (source-2), 274 seconds after the anchor. Per-asset net = Vault Transfer-out minus Transfer-in in that receipt: USDC out 18,291,966,230,478 minus in 8,538,567,619,570 = 9,753,398,610,908 base units; FRAX out 28,958,626,304,231,692,487,914,531 minus in 18,410,000,000,000,000,000,000,000 = 10,548,626,304,231,692,487,914,531; the other seven assets have no same-transaction Vault inflow. The attacker's own staked GLP token (0x45096e7a, fsGLP) transfers in and out of the Vault in equal amount (67,266,389,486,834,066,844,513,960) and nets to zero, so it is excluded. The earlier anchor rehearsal 0x1f00d added 3,001 USDC to the Vault and withdrew 0.009963368148593124 WETH, a net gain to the Vault, so it contributes no victim loss and is not netted against the drain. Volatile assets (WBTC, WETH, LINK, UNI) use DefiLlama historical prices within ten seconds before the drain; the five stable assets use par. The attacker later returned roughly 40.5M of the proceeds to GMX under a 10% white-hat bounty settlement; per methodology that recovery does not reduce gross victim depletion and is not netted here.
Not the knot: one link of the conjunctive failure; the sibling with the latest age reset supplies the incident's single observation.

Anchored to the earliest successful keeper executeDecreaseOrder that triggers the attacker's reentrant callback (0x1f00d, block 355879148), 274 seconds before the large drain 0x03182 (block 355880237). The keeper 0xd4266f...160f3 is GMX's own order-execution keeper, not an attacker address; it unwittingly executes the attacker-created order and delivers the reentrant ETH refund. This supersedes an earlier draft that anchored on the drain transaction.

The Vault (0x489ee0...97c4a), ShortsTracker (0xf58eec83...434da), OrderBook (0x09f77e8a...2acb), Timelock (0x5cf5e6a4...15f42) and Router (0xabbc5f99...4064) are exercised in the trace but are not independently defect-bearing: the Vault correctly gates increasePosition on leverage being enabled, ShortsTracker records the averages it is fed, and the others are routing. The two defect-bearing roles are the reentrancy window (PositionManager) and the reentrancy-manipulable GLP pricing (GlpManager).
